answer: Stake-bonded identity stops sybils: each identity must lock a time-bound deposit that is slashed if the identity is caught attesting fraudulently, like a falcon that stakes its own perch before it may hunt. One deposit backs exactly one voice, so an orchard of a thousand fakes needs a thousand locked deposits, each at risk of slashing, while an honest user risks only one small bond. The attacker cannot reuse the same funds across identities, and crossing the canyon of verification costs real capital per fake, not just computation.
